raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-AFW-HealthSecurityPhase3",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Delay in recruiting required specialists (accountant, environmental, gender‑based violence, etc.) may postpone PIU set‑up and hinder project start‑up.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Prepare a recruitment timetable, offer competitive contracts, and assign senior staff to monitor hiring progress.",
      "evidence": "CEMAC financing agreement (Section I.A.1b) requires appointment of specialists within 1 month of effective date."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Failure to customize accounting software within three months could impair financial tracking and reporting.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Engage IT vendor early, set clear milestones, and conduct weekly progress reviews.",
      "evidence": "Financing agreements (e.g., CEMAC Section I.A.1c, Cameroon Section I.A.2b) mandate software customization within 3 months."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Procurement delays and weak contract management in fragile settings may cause cost overruns and missed deadlines.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Hire experienced procurement specialists, provide World Bank procurement training, and use flexible procurement methods for FCV contexts.",
      "evidence": "Procurement Risks include delays, governance issues, weak contract management; mitigation measures listed in section 64‑66."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Environmental hazards from construction and laboratory waste could affect surrounding communities.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement site‑specific ESMPs, follow the National Healthcare Waste Management Plan, and monitor waste disposal.",
      "evidence": "Environmental risks listed as substantial (sections 65‑66); waste, dust, emissions, occupational health mentioned."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA/SH) risk due to increased community health workers and frontline staff.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Conduct GBV/SEA risk assessments, recruit GBV specialists, and train all staff on SEA/SH protocols.",
      "evidence": "SEA/SH risks judged substantial; mitigation includes GBV specialists and action plans (sections 72‑73)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Political instability and conflict in Cameroon, CAR, Chad and RoC may disrupt service delivery and field activities.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Develop security risk assessments, maintain flexible implementation schedules, and coordinate closely with the Regional Coordination Committee.",
      "evidence": "Regional context notes conflict, FCV, IDPs (section 2‑3); annexes describe ongoing insecurity."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Climate‑related shocks (floods, heat) could damage health facilities and increase disease burden.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Design health‑facility upgrades with green, resilient standards and integrate climate data into surveillance systems.",
      "evidence": "Climate change impacts described in sections 11‑12 and 37; green‑resilient approaches required."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Limited domestic fiscal space may reduce long‑term sustainability of health‑security investments.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Support medium‑term expenditure frameworks, domestic resource mobilization, and public‑private partnership pilots.",
      "evidence": "Sustainability discussion highlights need for domestic budgeting and resource tracking (section 48‑49)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Inadequate cross‑border data sharing could limit early detection of outbreaks.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Strengthen the RCC, finalize MoUs with WAHO, and adopt standardized data‑exchange protocols.",
      "evidence": "Regional coordination mechanisms and MoU requirements outlined in sections 30‑31 and 57."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Gender gap in technical health workforce may reduce effectiveness of surveillance and response.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement gender‑targeted recruitment, flexible training formats, and mentorship for women in epidemiology and veterinary fields.",
      "evidence": "Gender analysis and actions described in sections 75‑77."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Security threats to staff operating in conflict‑affected zones could cause injuries or project stoppage.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Prepare Security Risk Assessments, Security Management Plans, and provide safety training and evacuation procedures.",
      "evidence": "Security Risk Assessment and SMP to be prepared (section 73‑74)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Late submission of annual work plans and budgets may delay fund disbursement.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Set internal deadlines 30 days before the World Bank deadline and use a tracking tool for approvals.",
      "evidence": "Legal covenants require draft work plan by Nov 30 each year (Section I.C.1)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Inadequate stakeholder engagement could exclude vulnerable groups and generate grievances.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Deploy the Umbrella Stakeholder Engagement Plan, conduct community consultations, and operate functional GRMs.",
      "evidence": "Stakeholder engagement risks noted in sections 65‑66 and 71‑74."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Substantial fiduciary risk (FM residual risk rated Substantial) may lead to mis‑allocation of funds.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Update FM manuals, recruit internal and external auditors, and conduct quarterly internal audits.",
      "evidence": "FM residual risk assessed as Substantial; mitigation actions listed in sections 58‑60."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Limited procurement capacity (only one specialist) may hinder timely acquisition of goods and services.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Provide procurement capacity‑building workshops and consider joint procurement to share workload.",
      "evidence": "Procurement capacity described in section 62‑64; only one specialist and assistant noted."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R16",
      "description": "Laboratory capacity shortfalls (accreditation, equipment) could delay pathogen detection and response.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement SLIPTA quality improvement, QMS mentoring, and procure essential equipment per sub‑component 2.2 plans.",
      "evidence": "Laboratory quality and capacity sub‑component details (sections 30‑33) and SLIPTA targets."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Delay in recruiting required specialists (accountant, environmental, gender‑based violence, etc.) may postpone PIU set‑up and hinder project start‑up.
risks.mitigation: Prepare a recruitment timetable, offer competitive contracts, and assign senior staff to monitor hiring progress.
risks.evidence: CEMAC financing agreement (Section I.A.1b) requires appointment of specialists within 1 month of effective date.

risks.description: Failure to customize accounting software within three months could impair financial tracking and reporting.
risks.mitigation: Engage IT vendor early, set clear milestones, and conduct weekly progress reviews.
risks.evidence: Financing agreements (e.g., CEMAC Section I.A.1c, Cameroon Section I.A.2b) mandate software customization within 3 months.

risks.description: Procurement delays and weak contract management in fragile settings may cause cost overruns and missed deadlines.
risks.mitigation: Hire experienced procurement specialists, provide World Bank procurement training, and use flexible procurement methods for FCV contexts.
risks.evidence: Procurement Risks include delays, governance issues, weak contract management; mitigation measures listed in section 64‑66.

risks.description: Environmental hazards from construction and laboratory waste could affect surrounding communities.
risks.mitigation: Implement site‑specific ESMPs, follow the National Healthcare Waste Management Plan, and monitor waste disposal.
risks.evidence: Environmental risks listed as substantial (sections 65‑66); waste, dust, emissions, occupational health mentioned.

risks.description: Sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA/SH) risk due to increased community health workers and frontline staff.
risks.mitigation: Conduct GBV/SEA risk assessments, recruit GBV specialists, and train all staff on SEA/SH protocols.
risks.evidence: SEA/SH risks judged substantial; mitigation includes GBV specialists and action plans (sections 72‑73).

risks.description: Political instability and conflict in Cameroon, CAR, Chad and RoC may disrupt service delivery and field activities.
risks.mitigation: Develop security risk assessments, maintain flexible implementation schedules, and coordinate closely with the Regional Coordination Committee.
risks.evidence: Regional context notes conflict, FCV, IDPs (section 2‑3); annexes describe ongoing insecurity.

risks.description: Climate‑related shocks (floods, heat) could damage health facilities and increase disease burden.
risks.mitigation: Design health‑facility upgrades with green, resilient standards and integrate climate data into surveillance systems.
risks.evidence: Climate change impacts described in sections 11‑12 and 37; green‑resilient approaches required.

risks.description: Limited domestic fiscal space may reduce long‑term sustainability of health‑security investments.
risks.mitigation: Support medium‑term expenditure frameworks, domestic resource mobilization, and public‑private partnership pilots.
risks.evidence: Sustainability discussion highlights need for domestic budgeting and resource tracking (section 48‑49).

risks.description: Inadequate cross‑border data sharing could limit early detection of outbreaks.
risks.mitigation: Strengthen the RCC, finalize MoUs with WAHO, and adopt standardized data‑exchange protocols.
risks.evidence: Regional coordination mechanisms and MoU requirements outlined in sections 30‑31 and 57.

risks.description: Gender gap in technical health workforce may reduce effectiveness of surveillance and response.
risks.mitigation: Implement gender‑targeted recruitment, flexible training formats, and mentorship for women in epidemiology and veterinary fields.
risks.evidence: Gender analysis and actions described in sections 75‑77.

risks.description: Security threats to staff operating in conflict‑affected zones could cause injuries or project stoppage.
risks.mitigation: Prepare Security Risk Assessments, Security Management Plans, and provide safety training and evacuation procedures.
risks.evidence: Security Risk Assessment and SMP to be prepared (section 73‑74).

risks.description: Late submission of annual work plans and budgets may delay fund disbursement.
risks.mitigation: Set internal deadlines 30 days before the World Bank deadline and use a tracking tool for approvals.
risks.evidence: Legal covenants require draft work plan by Nov 30 each year (Section I.C.1).

risks.description: Inadequate stakeholder engagement could exclude vulnerable groups and generate grievances.
risks.mitigation: Deploy the Umbrella Stakeholder Engagement Plan, conduct community consultations, and operate functional GRMs.
risks.evidence: Stakeholder engagement risks noted in sections 65‑66 and 71‑74.

risks.description: Substantial fiduciary risk (FM residual risk rated Substantial) may lead to mis‑allocation of funds.
risks.mitigation: Update FM manuals, recruit internal and external auditors, and conduct quarterly internal audits.
risks.evidence: FM residual risk assessed as Substantial; mitigation actions listed in sections 58‑60.

risks.description: Limited procurement capacity (only one specialist) may hinder timely acquisition of goods and services.
risks.mitigation: Provide procurement capacity‑building workshops and consider joint procurement to share workload.
risks.evidence: Procurement capacity described in section 62‑64; only one specialist and assistant noted.

risks.description: Laboratory capacity shortfalls (accreditation, equipment) could delay pathogen detection and response.
risks.mitigation: Implement SLIPTA quality improvement, QMS mentoring, and procure essential equipment per sub‑component 2.2 plans.
risks.evidence: Laboratory quality and capacity sub‑component details (sections 30‑33) and SLIPTA targets.
